annotations.description: The 7-card hand had 3 Forests, Llanowar Visionary (ramp + card draw on turn 3), Wildheart Invoker (solid turn 4 play), and Gargoyle Sentinel. While it lacks black mana, the hand curves out and Visionary draws a card to help find black sources. Craterhoof is a dead card early but a potential finisher. This is a functional Limited hand.
annotations.actionTaken: Chose to mulligan down to 6 cards
annotations.betterLine: Keep the 7-card hand. It has 3 lands, a good curve (T3 Visionary into T4 Invoker), card draw to find black sources, and a late-game finisher. Going to 6 risks a worse hand with fewer resources.

annotations.description: Mulliganed a keepable 7-card hand with 2 lands, a 1-drop, strong synergy (Vito + Nocturnal Feeder + Silversmote Ghoul), and a reasonable curve. While land-light, the hand functions well if a 3rd land is drawn within 1-2 turns, which is statistically likely (~70%+ chance). The synergy package is too strong to throw away for a random 6.
annotations.actionTaken: Chose to mulligan to 6 cards
annotations.betterLine: Keep the 7-card hand. Play Wily Bandar turn 1, hope to draw a 3rd land for Vito or Nocturnal Feeder on turn 3.

annotations.description: Playing Swamp as their first/only land when they have Thriving Grove and Thriving Moor available. With no castable spells this turn regardless (nothing costs just B), playing a tapland would have been free tempo-wise while providing dual-color access next turn. Their hand is heavily green (Kibo, Orangutan, Wily Bandar) making green mana critical.
annotations.actionTaken: Played Swamp (untapped but only produces B, with no B-only spells castable this turn)
annotations.betterLine: Play Thriving Grove (choosing black) or Thriving Moor (choosing green) to get dual-color mana next turn at no tempo cost, since nothing castable this turn anyway.

annotations.description: Cast Overgrown Battlement over Wall of Blossoms. Wall of Blossoms draws a card on entry, providing immediate card advantage. With no pressure from the opponent (just a tapped Swamp), the card draw is likely more valuable than the mana acceleration, especially since the information and options from the extra card could shape the next several turns better.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Overgrown Battlement for mana ramp
annotations.betterLine: Cast Wall of Blossoms to draw a card immediately, gaining card advantage when there's no urgency to ramp

annotations.description: Chose Blue for Thriving Grove's secondary color, but the deck appears to be Green/Black with no blue cards. This wastes the color-fixing ability of the land entirely.
annotations.actionTaken: Chose Blue as the secondary color for Thriving Grove
annotations.betterLine: Choose Black to enable casting Eternal Thirst and other black cards in the deck, since the card pool clearly includes black cards (Eternal Thirst, Thriving Moor).

annotations.description: MstMed Trash passed priority with no creatures on board when they could have cast Wily Bandar for just {G}, developing board presence. Having a creature enables future Eternal Thirst, starts a clock, and is a free investment with no downside. With zero creatures against an opponent developing their board, every tempo point matters.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without casting any spells, ending the turn with no board development.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Wily Bandar for {G}, establishing board presence. Next turn they could play Swamp, cast Kibo or Uktabi Orangutan, and start building a meaningful board.

annotations.description: Passed the postcombat main phase without casting Wily Bandar, a free 1/1 creature. MstMed has no creatures on board while the opponent has a developed board with multiple creatures. Wily Bandar is a Monkey that synergizes with Kibo (in hand) and could be enchanted with Eternal Thirst on a future turn. There's no downside to deploying it here.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority with 1 mana available and Wily Bandar castable, ending the turn with no board presence.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Wily Bandar for {G} to establish board presence, create a Monkey for future Kibo synergy, and have a creature available for Eternal Thirst or blocking.

annotations.description: Activated Portcullis Vine to draw a card, sacrificing a defender, when Towering Titan was castable this turn. Before activating, they had 7+ mana available (3 lands + Archdruid for 1G + Overgrown Battlement for 3G) and Towering Titan costs 6. The Titan would have entered as a 13/13 (total toughness of other creatures: Portcullis Vine 3 + Overgrown Battlement 4 + Wall of Blossoms 4 + Elvish Archdruid 2 = 13). After sacrificing Portcullis Vine and spending 2 mana, they can no longer cast the Titan this turn, and it will be 3 counters smaller when eventually cast.
annotations.actionTaken: Activated Portcullis Vine to sacrifice a defender and draw a card for {2}
annotations.betterLine: Cast Towering Titan as a 13/13 using Elvish Archdruid, Overgrown Battlement, and lands for mana. This creates an enormous threat that likely wins the game against an opponent with no board presence.

annotations.description: Attacking with Elvish Archdruid for 2 damage against a 20-life opponent with no blockers, but this taps the Archdruid and prevents casting Gargoyle Sentinel (3 mana) or Ghirapur Guide (2G) in the post-combat main phase. With Thriving Grove + unplayed Forest + Archdruid tap = 3 mana available if Archdruid stayed back. Deploying a 3/3 Gargoyle Sentinel (adding toughness for Towering Titan) or a 3/2 Ghirapur Guide (another Elf for Archdruid synergy) is worth more than 2 chip damage.
annotations.actionTaken: Attacked with Elvish Archdruid for 2 damage
annotations.betterLine: Skip attacks, then in post-combat main play Forest and tap Thriving Grove + Forest + Archdruid to cast Gargoyle Sentinel or Ghirapur Guide, building board presence and toughness for the Towering Titan in hand.

annotations.description: Cast Kibo before playing a land. Playing Swamp first would give 4 mana total, allowing the possibility of casting both Kibo and Wily Bandar in the same turn (depending on Thriving Moor's chosen color). Playing land before spells is fundamental sequencing.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Kibo, Uktabi Prince without playing a land first
annotations.betterLine: Play Swamp first to have 4 mana available, then cast Kibo, Uktabi Prince, and potentially Wily Bandar with remaining mana

annotations.description: Sacrificed Portcullis Vine (3 toughness) before casting Towering Titan, which enters with +1/+1 counters equal to total toughness of other creatures. With Forest in hand to play post-combat, they could have cast Towering Titan as a 9/9 (Archdruid 2 + Vine 3 + Wall 4) instead of a 6/6 (Archdruid 2 + Wall 4). Losing 3 counters on Towering Titan is a significant cost for drawing one card, especially when the Vine could be sacrificed later.
annotations.actionTaken: Activated Portcullis Vine during combat, sacrificing a defender to draw a card before casting Towering Titan.
annotations.betterLine: Play Forest post-combat, cast Towering Titan as a 9/9 using Elvish Archdruid + 5 lands, then later sacrifice Portcullis Vine if needed (or use Titan's own sacrifice-defender ability for trample).

annotations.description: Activating Kibo's Banana-creating ability pre-combat taps Kibo, preventing it from attacking this turn. Kibo's attack trigger forces the defending player to sacrifice an artifact, which would trigger Kibo's +1/+1 counter ability if the opponent had a Banana. By creating Bananas now and tapping Kibo, the opponent gets a free Banana (ramp + 2 life) without being pressured to sacrifice it.
annotations.actionTaken: Activated Kibo's Banana-creating ability in precombat main phase, tapping Kibo
annotations.betterLine: Play Swamp, cast Simian Brawler or other creatures, then attack with Kibo (forcing opponent to sac an artifact if they have one). Activate Kibo's Banana ability post-combat if desired, or skip it entirely since giving the opponent resources without immediate payoff is questionable.

annotations.description: Activating Treetop Village for a temporary 3/3 attacker uses 2 mana that could be better spent deploying permanent threats. With a land drop available (Swamp in hand), MstMed could cast Simian Brawler (3/3 Ape Warrior) for {3}{G}, putting a permanent 3/3 body on the board that also synergizes with Kibo's Ape/Monkey counter ability. Against an opponent at 20 life, temporary damage is less valuable than board development.
annotations.actionTaken: Activated Treetop Village to make it a 3/3 attacker for the turn
annotations.betterLine: Play Swamp from hand, then cast Simian Brawler ({3}{G}) to develop a permanent 3/3 Ape creature that synergizes with Kibo. Could still attack with Kibo next turn to force artifact sacrifice.

annotations.description: Player passed their entire precombat main phase with a land drop available (Swamp in hand), castable spells (Eternal Thirst, Wily Bandar), and Uktabi Orangutan that could destroy the opponent's Banana token. Passing here ends the turn without deploying any resources, wasting an entire turn's development.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority in precombat main phase, effectively ending the turn with no plays.
annotations.betterLine: Play Swamp first, then cast Eternal Thirst on Kibo (giving it lifelink and growth potential), or cast Uktabi Orangutan targeting opponent's Banana token (which would also trigger Kibo's +1/+1 counter ability for Apes/Monkeys). At the very least, play the land and cast Wily Bandar to develop the board.

annotations.description: Passed the turn with a land drop available and enough mana to cast Towering Titan as a 5/5, or alternatively Gargoyle Sentinel or Ghirapur Guide. The player had 4 untapped lands + Elvish Archdruid, and playing a Forest would give exactly 6 mana ({4}{G}{G}) for Towering Titan, which would enter as a 5/5 (total toughness of Archdruid 2 + Portcullis Vine 3). Instead, they passed doing nothing, wasting an entire turn's worth of development against an opponent with a weak board.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority in precombat main phase with land drop available and multiple castable spells in hand.
annotations.betterLine: Play Forest, then cast Towering Titan for {4}{G}{G} (using 5 lands + Elvish Archdruid). Titan enters as a 5/5 with the option to sacrifice Portcullis Vine for mass trample. This creates a dominant board position against opponent's lone Kibo.

annotations.description: Passed priority in postcombat main with a land drop available, multiple castable creatures in hand, and enough mana to deploy threats. Could have played a Forest and cast Gargoyle Sentinel (setting up a huge Towering Titan next turn) or even attempted to cast Towering Titan this turn using Elvish Archdruid and Banana token for mana. Wasted an entire turn's worth of development while behind on board.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority, ending the turn with no plays.
annotations.betterLine: Play a Forest, then cast Gargoyle Sentinel (3/3 defender) to build board presence and set up Towering Titan for next turn. Alternatively, play Forest and attempt to cast Towering Titan this turn using Archdruid + Banana for the 6th and 7th mana.

annotations.description: Activating Kibo's tap ability creates Banana tokens for both players, giving the opponent resources while tapping Kibo so it can't attack. The opponent already has a Banana token. Attacking with Kibo would force the opponent to sacrifice that Banana, triggering Kibo's +1/+1 counter ability on all your Apes/Monkeys. Additionally, Uktabi Orangutan could destroy the opponent's Banana before combat for additional counter triggers.
annotations.actionTaken: Activated Kibo's tap ability to create Banana tokens for both players, tapping Kibo.
annotations.betterLine: Play Swamp (land drop), cast Uktabi Orangutan targeting opponent's Banana token (triggering Kibo's counter ability on all Apes/Monkeys), then attack with Kibo to force another artifact sacrifice.

annotations.description: Should play the Swamp land before casting Uktabi Orangutan. Playing land before spells is correct sequencing - it preserves information and ensures the land drop isn't forgotten. While the Swamp doesn't help cast Orangutan this turn, having an extra land in play could matter for future turns and there's no downside to playing it first.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Uktabi Orangutan without first playing the Swamp from hand.
annotations.betterLine: Play Swamp first, then cast Uktabi Orangutan. The Orangutan play itself is good (destroys opponent's Banana token, triggers Kibo for +1/+1 counters on Apes/Monkeys), but land should come down first.

annotations.description: Animated Treetop Village to get Kibo's +1/+1 counter on it, but the counter on a land that costs mana to animate each turn is less valuable than deploying Wily Bandar (a permanent creature) which would also receive the counter from Kibo's trigger.
annotations.actionTaken: Activated Treetop Village's animation ability to make it an Ape and receive Kibo's +1/+1 counter
annotations.betterLine: Play Swamp from hand, tap Treetop Village for {G}, cast Wily Bandar ({G}) to have it on the battlefield as a Cat Monkey when Kibo's trigger resolves, getting a permanent 2/2 creature with the counter instead

annotations.description: Player passed in postcombat main with 2 untapped lands and two castable spells. Eternal Thirst could be cast on Kibo (a growing 3/3 with lifelink would be very strong), or at minimum Wily Bandar (a Monkey with Kibo synergy) could be deployed for free. Both represent meaningful board development left on the table.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority, ending the turn without casting anything.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Eternal Thirst on Kibo, Uktabi Prince using Treetop Village and Swamp. This gives Kibo lifelink and +1/+1 counter growth when opponent's creatures die, significantly increasing its threat level. Alternatively, at minimum cast Wily Bandar as a free Monkey body with Kibo synergy.

annotations.description: GptOSS Nature passed priority with Kibo's 'sacrifice an artifact' trigger on the stack. They could have tapped the Banana token for {G} and 2 life (sacrificing it), then tapped Forest for {G}, and activated Portcullis Vine ({2}, tap, sacrifice a defender) to draw a card. This would have converted the Banana (which would be lost to Kibo's trigger anyway) into 2 life and a card draw via Portcullis Vine sacrifice.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority, letting the Banana token be sacrificed for nothing to Kibo's trigger.
annotations.betterLine: Tap Banana for {G} and 2 life, tap Forest for {G}, activate Portcullis Vine (pay {2}, tap, sacrifice itself) to draw a card. Lose a blocker but gain a card and 2 life while denying Kibo's trigger any meaningful sacrifice.

annotations.description: By passing on Kibo's trigger resolving without activating Treetop Village first, MstMed missed the opportunity to get a free +1/+1 counter on Treetop Village. Since Treetop Village becomes an Ape creature when activated, it would receive a +1/+1 counter from Kibo's 'Whenever an artifact an opponent controls is put into a graveyard' trigger. The counter persists permanently, making Treetop Village a 4/4 trampler every time it's animated in the future.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority, letting Kibo's trigger resolve without activating Treetop Village
annotations.betterLine: Activate Treetop Village for {1}{G} to make it a 3/3 Ape creature before Kibo's trigger resolves, gaining a permanent +1/+1 counter on it for free

annotations.description: Taking 8 damage from Kibo (4/4) and Uktabi Orangutan (4/4) with no blocks when Ghirapur Guide (4/3) could have traded with Kibo, killing the opponent's key engine piece that generates Banana tokens and pumps all Apes/Monkeys. Portcullis Vine could also have chump-blocked the Orangutan to save 4 additional life. Instead, GptOSS drops to 9 life and leaves Kibo alive to continue snowballing.
annotations.actionTaken: Declared no blockers, taking 8 damage (17 → 9 life) and leaving Kibo alive.
annotations.betterLine: Block Kibo with Ghirapur Guide (both die in combat, removing the opponent's engine) and optionally block Uktabi Orangutan with Portcullis Vine to save 4 life. This would result in taking only 0-4 damage while eliminating the most dangerous opposing creature.

annotations.description: Passed the entire precombat main phase with an unplayed land drop, multiple castable creatures (Simian Brawler, Wily Bandar), Eternal Thirst available, and Kibo's tap ability unused. Opponent is at 9 life with 10 power on board - developing further before combat could enable lethal or near-lethal attacks. The Forest land drop alone is free value, and casting Simian Brawler (another Ape for Kibo synergy) adds significant pressure.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority in precombat main phase, doing nothing
annotations.betterLine: Play Forest, activate Kibo to create Banana tokens, cast Simian Brawler (3/3 Ape), cast Wily Bandar, then potentially put Eternal Thirst on Kibo or Orangutan for lifelink, then move to combat with a much stronger board
